content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary cluster us-west-2 | model=redwood-small-v1 | 5x increase in 5xx error rate since deploy at 21:04 UTC. Affected routes: /v1/generate. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/telemetry/canary/2145882233
Alex: I'm oncall, taking this. pinging deploy for the recent rollout.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-14T21:02Z triggered: commit `c3f1a9b` by Julia. Canary rollout 3/5 pods. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/7321
Alex: quick check of logs shows a spike in tokenizer errors (runtime panics) coming from tokenstream length calc.
Julia: I authored that commit — small tokenizer edge-case fix for rare unicode sequences. I ran unit tests but didn't exercise long multi-byte inputs.
Ben: canary is failing fast, looks like a single commit regression. Suggest revert that single commit to stop the outage.
Alice: support seeing increased error reports from EU customers via Intercom. Need impact numbers before we notify CSMs.
Alex: grabbing metrics now.
Alex: quick impact assessment: approx 2.1% of generation requests in canary zone are 5xx. Latency unaffected for successful requests. No signs of data leakage.
Eve: mark severity P2 for now. If rollback reduces errors to normal, we'll keep that.
Ben: recommend kill-switch feature-flag for new tokenizer until revert is live. We can flip flag via FF service but commit revert is faster.
Julia: if revert is straightforward I'm happy to own it.
Alex: prepping single-commit revert and quick patch release. Running the revert locally then will push hotfix to canary first.
Alex: commands I'm running:
```bash
# create revert commit
git checkout main && git pull origin main
git revert --no-edit c3f1a9b
git push origin main
# trigger canary rollout via infra pipeline
ci trigger deploy --env canary --tag hotfix/revert-c3f1a9b
```
Ben: also flip canary routing to healthy pool as safety: `routerctl set-weight canary-us-west-2 0.3` (taking traffic down from 1.0 to 0.3)
deploy-bot: Pipeline started: hotfix/revert-c3f1a9b. Build 553 triggered.
Alex: build passed, rolling out to canary pods now.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed for hotfix/revert-c3f1a9b at 21:14 UTC.
incident-bot: Monitoring window started (10m) after new canary.
Alex: initial telemetry shows 5xx rate dropping back toward baseline. Pushing to additional canary nodes to validate.
Alice: provisional customer impact: ~120 tickets generated, mostly retryable user errors. Preparing standard customer note template.
Julia: quick root cause: my tokenizer code did an unchecked slice on a byte sequence — edge-case with mixed zero-width joiners. PR coming to add guard + unit/regression tests.
Ben: good — please add a dedicated fuzz test for multibyte sequences in the tokenizer suite.
Alex: rolling revert to all canary shards now, will promote to prod after 30m stable window.
deploy-bot: Prod promotion scheduled: canary->prod after 30m stable.
incident-bot: Error rate back to baseline on canary: 21:22 UTC. 10m window looks clean.
Alice: sending customer-facing note to CSMs: "Service briefly returned 5xx for a small percentage of generation requests in us-west-2 after a canary deploy. Fix applied and services are stable. No customer data was exposed."
Eve: please file a postmortem and assign action items: owner of revert, added tests, improve canary throttle. Severity confirmed P2.
Alex: creating incident ticket and will hand off to Dmitri for overnight follow-up. Dmitri, you're up for the post-deploy watch.
Dmitri: acknowledged, taking handoff. I'll monitor the 6AM UTC report and verify prod promotion metrics.
Julia: will open a PR with proper guard + tests and reference this incident.
Ben: followups: (1) automated fuzz harness for tokenizer, (2) stricter canary traffic cap by default, (3) add an extra expo backoff on tokenizer ops for long inputs.
Alice: I notified CSMs and queued a customer email draft for legal review.
Eve: thanks team. We'll collate logs and put together 1hr blameless postmortem draft tomorrow. Good recovery. :white_check_mark:
